meaning: Mean wall thickness; the range covers 90% of the wall area.
Share of the bounding volume filled with material.
Surface area packed into each unit of part volume (higher = more surface to finish, coat or exchange through).
Surface area per unit of solid material (same quantity as the STL tool's S/V).
Radius of the sphere that bends like the surface does (1/curvedness). Point-based, same information as the STL tool.
Share of surface facing downward more steeply than the overhang limit (typically the roughest in AM).
How far you move along the surface before its bending changes by about its own typical amount (typical curvature / typical mean-curvature gradient). Short = rapidly varying curvature.
Typical radius of the sideways turns the lines of curvature make within the surface (small = sharp steering). Evaluated over the whole surface, so no sampling noise.
1 = runs straight, 0 = comes back to where it started. Net progress per distance travelled.
1 = runs straight, 0 = comes back to where it started. Net progress per distance travelled.
Share of line length twisting right minus share twisting left. 0 = balanced (mirror-symmetric); +-1 = all one way. Point-curvature statistics cannot see this.
Geometry-only uniformity factor eps/(a_v (N_field L)^2): compare designs without bath data. Higher = more even coating.
Coating uniformity. High = interior plates nearly as thick as the outside; low = current crowds onto the faces nearest the anode (paper: Octet 0.86 ~2x, IsoTruss 0.24 ~4.6x top-to-bottom).
Plating speed limit": the highest average current that still meets the target uniformity."
